Look for repeated tracking through solid: Look for repeated tracking through solid cover, pre-aiming unseen positions and reactions without visual, sound or teammate information. A wallbang or smoke kill by itself is not proof.

Look for repeated small magnetic-looking: Look for repeated small magnetic-looking corrections, unusually consistent micro-adjustments and the crosshair being pulled onto targets at the last moment across many encounters.
Automation that fires the weapon when an: Automation that fires the weapon when an opponent enters the crosshair, without needing the player to press fire at that moment.
Look for repeated shots at almost identi: Look for repeated shots at almost identical zero-delay timing when enemies cross a held angle. One fast reaction is not enough; the pattern should repeat.
Assistance that exposes enemy locations: Assistance that exposes enemy locations on a radar or separate overlay even when the game should not reveal them.
Look for repeated rotations, counters an: Look for repeated rotations, counters and positioning around unseen opponents without sound, teammate calls or legitimate radar information, especially across several rounds.
A script or assistance that removes reco: A script or assistance that removes recoil or automates the mouse movement needed to control a weapon spray.
Look for repeated sprays with absent or: Look for repeated sprays with absent or nearly identical recoil correction over many bursts. Skilled recoil control or one clean spray is not proof by itself.
Automation that times jumps or strafing: Automation that times jumps or strafing inputs to maintain bunny-hop movement with minimal manual error.
Look for long, repeated sequences of nea: Look for long, repeated sequences of near-perfect jump timing and speed retention. A short successful sequence can happen legitimately.
Manipulation of the player model or view: Manipulation of the player model or viewing angles intended to make the real orientation or hit position difficult to read.
Look for repeated impossible-looking ang: Look for repeated impossible-looking angles, rapid spinning, severe model desynchronisation or orientation that does not match the player's movement and shots.
Assistance or exploitation that creates: Assistance or exploitation that creates controlled teleport-like, desynchronised or otherwise abnormal movement.
Look for the abnormal movement recurring: Look for the abnormal movement recurring in the player's favour while other players and the server remain stable. General network lag affecting everyone is not the same thing.
Switching cheating assistance on and off: Switching cheating assistance on and off during a match, often to make suspicious moments appear intermittent.
Look for repeated abrupt changes in awar: Look for repeated abrupt changes in awareness, accuracy or automation followed by equally abrupt returns to normal play. Ordinary performance variation is not enough.
Suspicious gameplay assistance that does: Suspicious gameplay assistance that does not fit one of the more specific categories.

An automated account that remains in mat: An automated account that remains in matches to obtain XP, drops or other rewards without normal human participation.
Look for fixed routes, repetitive action: Look for fixed routes, repetitive actions, identical reaction timing, failure to respond normally and accounts that freeze or leave when spectated. Check for a pattern, not just one AFK player.
A coordinated group of automated account: A coordinated group of automated accounts that fills or controls a server and removes human players through vote-kicks.
Look for many accounts behaving similarl: Look for many accounts behaving similarly, coordinated or immediate votes, repeated removal of human players and the server returning to automated activity afterwards.
